newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian port chaos as French road strike continues.
newsitem.headline: Belgian port chaos as French road strike continues.

text.p: Lorries forced to detour through the Belgian port of Zeebrugge by the French road hauliers strike faced massive tailbacks on Wednesday and 20-hour waiting times to board ferries.

"It is totally blocked. There are more than 1,000 trucks and more coming," a spokesman for the port gendarmerie told Reuters by telephone. "They can't get through Calais so they are all coming here on the way to Dover."
A spokesman for the harbour masters' office said drivers were having to wait up to 20 hours to board ships bound for Britain.
In Belgium's other main gateway to Britain, Ostend, a spokesman for the gendarmerie said everything was calm.
On Tuesday a spokesman for the ferry company Stena-Sally Lines reported booming business as trucks headed for Britain were rerouted from the blockaded port at Calais to Ostend on route to Ramsgate.
"All our sailings are fully booked with freight lorries," he said. "Normally at this time of year they are only half full."
A spokesman for the Belgian Transport Association said on Tuesday the French strike, now in its 10th day, was costing Belgian haulage firms millions of francs.
"It is impossible to get to Spain by road at all, and getting to Italy you have to detour through Luxembourg, Germany and Switzerland which has a 28-tonne weight limit," he told Reuters.
He said the association had advised its members to avoid France, but said about 70 trucks were still trapped there.
"The situation is getting worse hour by hour. The strike is costing hauliers tens of millions of francs," he added.
The strike is also begining to affect Belgian industry.

De Standaard newspaper reported on Wednesday that the Belgian plant of French car maker Renault had been forced to shut its doors temporarily because supplies of parts for assembly were stranded in France.
